title: Bounded Byzantine book states: Greek, Ruthenian, Vulgata and early Slavonic witnesses

traditions.label: Early Greek euchologion witnesses
traditions.scope: Greek manuscript states relevant to later Byzantine history
traditions.coverage_note: One catalogue-identified witness; no continuous stemma to Roman Greek editions.

traditions.label: Roman Greek Euchologion
traditions.scope: Greek books corrected and issued under Roman authority
traditions.coverage_note: 1754 state described by its governing act; original scan and later edition collation missing.

traditions.label: Sinai Slavonic mixed liturgical collection
traditions.scope: The Sinaitic Liturgiarium with Greek-derived and Latin-derived material
traditions.coverage_note: Not a declared ancestor of Ruthenian or Vulgata books. Separate copying and later additions.

traditions.label: Ruthenian Slavonic books and Roman revision
traditions.scope: Eucharistic rubrics and complementary books, with regional reception limits
traditions.coverage_note: 1692/1733 and 1905/1940–1942 clusters; gaps between them are not silently connected.

traditions.label: Roman Slavonic Vulgata (Russian-use series)
traditions.scope: Russian-use Chrysostom book, full Sluzhebnik and calendar supplement
traditions.coverage_note: Parallel to Ruthenian series; not its successor or derivative. Intended audience is not proof of universal reception.

sources.title: Pinakes, Diktyon 64879: Vatican Barberini gr. 336
sources.inspection: Directly fetched HTML; contents/date/provenance and Basil/Chrysostom folio entries read.
sources.limitations: Catalogue inspection, not manuscript text collation.

sources.title: Heinz Miklas, Excavating the Palimpsests in the Glagolitic Manuscripts from Sinai, pp. 217–230
sources.inspection: PDF fetched; page images 219, 222–223 inspected, especially notes 17, 52, 57–58.
sources.limitations: Author reconstruction; original multispectral manuscript images not inspected. Dates of overtext and later additions must remain separate.

sources.title: Benedict XIV, Ex quo primum, 1 March 1756
sources.inspection: Vatican HTML Italian body read, especially §§ 5–9 and § 17; saved exact HTML.
sources.limitations: Official translated delivery, despite Spanish URL. Greek 1754 book leaves not acquired. Historical claims inside the act are attributed to it.

sources.title: Congregation for the Eastern Church, circular I, Prot. 1219/28, 10 September 1941
sources.inspection: Complete displayed Ukrainian translated reproduction read, especially §§ 1–6 and final norms. Exact HTML saved.
sources.limitations: Later web reproduction labelled Ukrainian translation sent from Rome; original signed Italian instrument not inspected.

sources.title: Congregation for the Eastern Church, circular II, Prot. 1219/28, 10 September 1941
sources.inspection: Direct HTML fetched after web cache failure; entire Ukrainian reproduction read, particularly section I, numbered points 1–8, and section II.
sources.limitations: Original Italian and 1905/1940 book pages not inspected. This is primary-description through a translated reproduction, never text-collated evidence.

sources.title: Alphonsus Raes, Libri liturgici in lingua Slavica a Sancta Sede editi, 1947, pp. 85–88
sources.inspection: Downloaded journal; directly inspected printed pp. 85–88, physical PDF 91–94 as page images.
sources.limitations: Contemporary scholarly account; separate service-book pages not inspected. PDF container includes other material. Rights for redistribution not established.

sources.title: Ilya Semenenko-Basin and Stefano Caprio, Russian Liturgical Memories in the Slavic Byzantine-Catholic Menologion, Slověne 2021/1
sources.inspection: Downloaded PDF, text-layer search; directly inspected pp. 382–383, physical PDF 15–16, for 1942/1953 comparison.
sources.limitations: Authors’ book comparison, not this project’s collation; their 1953 source locator is second pagination pp. 47–48.

sources.title: Metropolitan Cantor Institute, The Liturgikon, or Služebnik
sources.inspection: Contents and Church Slavonic sections read; exact HTML retained and original online-book URL extracted.
sources.limitations: Undated institutional overview; its English-book currentness claims were not used. Historical scan link now returns 404.

sources.title: Google Books full-view record, Euchologion neosti meta typothen, 1754
sources.inspection: HTML fetched; title/date, fullview flag, page map and offered PDF route inspected. Pontifical Gregorian catalogue 51106BIB independently links this same ID.
sources.limitations: No book page image inspected. Download failed HTTP 429; no source-book payload acquired. Metadata establishes an acquisition target, not contents.

stages.label: Basil and Chrysostom in an early Greek euchologion
stages.scope: Identified manuscript contents, not a reconstructed complete medieval rite
stages.summary: Basil ff. 1–22v and Chrysostom ff. 23–43v; Basil has a catalogued lacuna.

evidence.claim: Dated s.08(2/2), copied in Calabria; identified Eucharistic sections.

stages.limitations: Copy date does not date composition. No predecessor/successor asserted.
stages.reception: Historical Greek witness; later Catholic reception of this exact text not established.

stages.label: Greek Euchologion with four prefatory instructions
stages.scope: Prefatory Eucharistic rubrics and editorial policy
stages.summary: Four introductory instructions; first directs papal and Catholic-hierarchy commemoration, with a marginal liturgical cross-reference.

evidence.claim: Names 1754 publication and the instructions; § 9 traces the commemoration provision to a confirmed 1746 decision.

stages.limitations: No claim that papal commemoration originated in 1754 (§ 17 discusses prior obligations); no before/after book collation.
stages.reception: Act addresses clergy of Greek rite in communion with Rome; actual territorial uptake not established.

stages.label: Sinai collection before Demetrius’s additions
stages.scope: Main overtext and identified component liturgies
stages.witness_label: Sinai, Sin. slav. NF 5, with Petersburg fragments BRAN 24.4.8 and RNB glag. 2
stages.summary: Contains Greek-derived Basil, Chrysostom and James material alongside a mixed Apollinaris liturgy.

evidence.claim: Dates overtext and identifies the formerly separated Petersburg portion and mixed contents.

stages.limitations: No direct manuscript collation; source describes a damaged, composite witness.
stages.reception: Sinai collection; no reception into a named modern Catholic recension asserted.

stages.label: Demetrius adds diptych material
stages.scope: Later additions within the same physical collection
stages.witness_label: Sinaitic Liturgiarium: Demetrius’s additions, especially RNB glag. 2
stages.summary: Later diptych includes Western names absent from the relevant main-text passage.

evidence.locus: p. 222, final Textology paragraph; p. 223 and nn. 57–58
evidence.claim: Dates Demetrius’s entries; identifies added diptych and omitted passage at main-part f. 17v.

stages.limitations: Proposed motive for the addition is the scholar’s inference. This is not a new whole-book edition.
stages.reception: Same composite Sinai witness; subsequent use and descent unestablished.

stages.label: Eucharistic rubrics codified at Vilnius
stages.scope: Rubrical layer retrospectively identified by the 1941 circular
stages.summary: Codified rubrics later expanded in the read-Liturgy order.

evidence.claim: Explicitly identifies the 1692 Vilnius codification.

stages.limitations: Existing catalogue row spans 1692–1695; this stage concerns only the named 1692 component. Exact book uninspected.
stages.reception: Circular reports unequal regional acceptance; no universal Ruthenian adoption claimed.

stages.label: Expanded order for the read Liturgy
stages.scope: Inserted order of celebration, not an entirely new anaphora
stages.witness_label: Univ Sluzhebnik, 1733, order for the read Liturgy
stages.summary: Expanded the earlier Eucharistic rubrics through a distinct inserted order.

evidence.claim: Names first insertion at Univ in 1733 and subsequent eighteenth-century reprinting.

stages.limitations: Individual source-book rubrics not collated; cannot assign every later practice to 1733.
stages.reception: Regional reception differed; nineteenth-century Galician omission and ceremonial survival are reported, not fully mapped.

stages.label: Lviv’s eight provisions for private celebration
stages.summary: Eight provisions are the explicit object of the later circular’s corrections.

evidence.claim: Identifies full Lviv 1905 Sluzhebnik and its eight provisions.
Identifies the 1905 book as widely used before Roman revision.

stages.limitations: Book’s own pages not acquired; no direct descent from Univ 1733 established.
stages.reception: Institution reports use in Europe and America; extent and uniformity not quantified.

stages.label: Revised Ruthenian Chrysostom book and implementation rules
stages.date_label: Attested by 10 September 1941 circulars; underlying Chrysostom book published 1940
stages.scope: Chrysostom text/rubrics, with separate implementing circulars
stages.witness_label: Sancta et divina Liturgia S. Joannis Chrysostomi, Rome, 1940; circulars I–II, 1941
stages.summary: Pre-epiclesis troparia omitted; private celebration follows common ceremonies with specified accommodations.

evidence.claim: Records omission and other qualified rubrics.
Explains changes from Lviv 1905.

stages.limitations: 1941 clarifications are not a separately asserted new printing. Whole book uncollated. The positioned date is the attestation of implementing rules, not a new 1941 printing or the start of universal use.
stages.reception: Circular I preserves territorial rules and older clergy’s private customary use; formation houses directed to new books.

stages.label: Full Ruthenian Liturgikon assembled
stages.scope: Complementary liturgies, daily offices and calendar material
stages.summary: Full volume gathers the previously issued components and supplementary/calendar material.

evidence.claim: Names the full volume and distinguishes Ruthenian feasts from Russian material.

stages.limitations: Assembly is not proof of changed Chrysostom wording; no 1940→1942 textual revision asserted.
stages.reception: Ruthenian recension; particular Churches’ actual adoption remains separately evidenced.

stages.label: Russian-use Chrysostom book
stages.witness_label: Divina Liturgia S. Joannis Chrysostomi, Rome 1940, 112 pages (Raes)
stages.summary: Papal commemoration replaces the Synod reference; pre-epiclesis troparia retained with optional omission.

evidence.claim: Explicitly contrasts Russian-use policy with Ruthenian § 2.

stages.limitations: Russian precursor printing unidentified; do not manufacture a Russian-Synodal predecessor node.
stages.reception: Prepared for Catholic clergy following Russian usage; not a Ruthenian successor.

stages.label: Full Russian-use Sluzhebnik assembled
stages.scope: Full service book with calendar and appendices
stages.summary: Complete volume with differentiated calendar and supplementary material.

evidence.claim: Identifies complete book and Russian commemorations.
Distinguishes the later addition from this calendar state.

stages.limitations: Assembly does not establish another revision of 1940 prayers.
stages.reception: Russian-use Catholic recension; Bulgarian/Serbian local receipt not shown here.

stages.label: All Saints of Rus added to calendar supplement
stages.scope: Named movable commemoration and its liturgical propers
stages.summary: Adds All Saints of Rus on the second Sunday after Pentecost with specified proper chants.

evidence.claim: Identifies addition and source-book locator.

stages.limitations: Exact 1953 pages not inspected; no claim of a complete edition diff.
stages.reception: Addition within the Catholic Vulgata publication; use frequency not established.

transitions.summary: Later hand supplements the collection’s diptych.

changes.before: Main Apollinaris copy omits the relevant passage.
changes.after: Demetrius adds a diptych including Mastal, Petrunia and Romald.
changes.locus_before: Sin. slav. NF5 f. 17v, as identified by Miklas

evidence.claim: Addition and main-copy omission identified.
Distinguishes copying from later entries.

transitions.limitations: No direct folio collation; reason for addition and name identifications remain attributed.

transitions.summary: The inserted read-Liturgy order expands the earlier codified rubrics.

evidence.claim: States codification followed by considerable expansion.
Retrospective authoritative sequence.

transitions.limitations: The circular reports expansion, but no named new prayer or rubric has been inspected. This is a revision proposal, not an established substantive transition; direct exemplar copying also remains unestablished.

transitions.summary: Roman clarification replaces selected private-celebration provisions and retains others.

changes.before: Proskomedia in sacristy under the first 1905 provision.
changes.after: Prothesis table and transfer to altar; constrained-altar accommodations.
changes.locus_before: Lviv 1905 point 1, quoted in circular II I.1

evidence.claim: Explicitly abolishes first provision.

changes.after: Common ceremonies: entrances, Gospel facing people, and ambon prayer outside Royal Doors, with accommodations.

evidence.claim: Specifies implementation rather than only announcing a new book.
Direct numbered treatment of predecessor provisions.

transitions.limitations: Not a line-by-line source-book collation. Do not generalize the private-celebration concessions to every solemn celebration. Continuity control: circular II I.5 expressly retains omission of the high-place ceremony in this context; it is not a change.

transitions.summary: Roman Greek rubrics supply a norm while older Ruthenian readings are preserved.

changes.after: Ruthenian revision uses it with local textual/rubrical qualifications.
changes.locus_before: 1754 Euchologion as named in circular I § 4

evidence.claim: Greek norm qualified by older Ruthenian evidence.
Affirms rubric relationship and preserved Ruthenian tradition.
Names Benedict XIV’s Greek book.

transitions.limitations: Reception of a stated norm, not whole-book translation or proof of identical wording. Older Ruthenian readings are not dated here.

transitions.summary: Component publication followed by assembled service volume; no new anaphora state inferred.

evidence.claim: Separate components precede complete 1942 volume.

transitions.limitations: A packaging/completeness relationship, not a substantive revision edge. The 1941 intermediate components remain within this set rather than artificial successive versions.

transitions.summary: Component publication followed by assembled service volume; no new anaphora state inferred.

evidence.claim: Separate components precede complete 1942 volume.

transitions.limitations: A packaging/completeness relationship, not a substantive revision edge. The 1941 intermediate components remain within this set rather than artificial successive versions.

transitions.summary: A movable commemoration and its proper chants enter the supplement.

changes.before: All Saints of Rus absent from the 1942 RVM.
changes.after: Second Sunday after Pentecost gains the commemoration.

evidence.claim: Explicit before/after statement.

changes.after: Matins/liturgy prokeimena, alleluia and communion verse; no individual saints list.

evidence.claim: Specifies supplied items.
Identifies reissued volume and added supplement.

transitions.limitations: Scholarly-described comparison, not independently text-collated. The article’s explanation of the changed Russian adjective is interpretive and is not promoted here.

gaps.consequence: Barberini must remain an isolated attested state, not a direct parent of 1754.

gaps.missing: Original 1754 monita/marginal rubric images, predecessor identity, and 1873 comparison.
gaps.next_source: Google Books B9BRAAAAcAAJ (full-view record; download failed 429); Gregorian University Ris.23 G8, catalogue 51106BIB; 1873 S.L.23 G4.
gaps.consequence: Only act-described 1754 contents established; no claimed 1754→1873 revision.

gaps.missing: Direct images of main and added diptychs; later transmission into identified books.
gaps.next_source: Sinai Palimpsests site item 82; Sin.slav.NF5 f. 17v; RNB glag.2; Miklas p. 223 nn. 57–58.
gaps.consequence: Cannot turn mixed Sinai witness into a Ruthenian/Vulgata ancestor.

gaps.missing: Exact intervening prayer/rubric states, including local uptake and survival.
gaps.next_source: Original Vilnius 1692, Univ 1733 and Lviv 1905 Sluzhebnik; Raes, Le Liturgicon ruthène depuis l’Union de Brest, OCP 8 (1942), 95–143.
gaps.consequence: No automatic chain across the unexamined centuries; no blanket Latinization/de-Latinization label.

gaps.missing: Source-language before/after leaves and original Italian circulars; exact 1944 Ordo departures.
gaps.next_source: OCP 8 (1942), printed 138–143 for circulars (search-discovered lead, not inspected); 1905 eight private-Liturgy points; Roman 1940/1942 books; Ordo 1944.
gaps.consequence: Changes are primary-described through translation, not text-collated. Ordo 1944 is not made a new whole-book stage.

gaps.missing: Exact Russian Synodal exemplar, original 1940/1942 pages, and 1953 added propers.
gaps.next_source: Roman Vulgata 1940 Chrysostom, 1942 Sluzhebnik; 1953 Sluzhebnik second pagination 47–48.
gaps.consequence: Specific policy and calendar addition established from descriptions; complete revision scope remains unknown.

gaps.missing: Local decrees/implementation accounts per Church and jurisdiction.
gaps.next_source: 1941 circular I final norms; diocesan/synodal archives; dated reception letters.
gaps.consequence: A common recension does not mean simultaneous universal replacement; old custom concessions must remain visible.
